text: Fig. 4.1 gives information about the eruption of Mount Tambora.
The largest volcanic eruption in human history took place in 1815 at Tambora, a
strato-volcano on Sumbawa Island in Indonesia. The eruption itself killed between 11 000
and 12 000 people, mainly by pyroclastic flows on the island. Parts of the island were
buried in ash over 1.5 m deep. Ash clouds from the eruption affected the weather in Europe
and North America, and the cool summer of 1816 resulted in crop failures and up to 70 000
